suggested_experiment_name: Axion relic density (misalignment, post-inflationary PQ breaking)
coupling_convention: Omega, axion relic density (dimensionless density parameter) exactly as plotted on the y-axis; x-axis is axion mass m_a converted from ueV to eV
notes: Theory paper assessing uncertainties in the temperature-dependent topological susceptibility chi(T) (instanton vs lattice QCD) and their impact on the QCD axion relic density from misalignment. It relates relic density to zero-temperature axion mass and misalignment angle (e.g., ma ~ 30 ueV benchmarks, Figs. 1-2), but presents NO experimental exclusion limit, no sensitivity projection, and no bound on any axion coupling or on the f_a-m_a plane. The results are relic-density predictions with a factor 2-3 uncertainty in ma, not constraints. Therefore no extractable limit data. | selector: figure_vision (sole candidate) | Vision: This is not a laboratory exclusion plot but a theoretical relic-density prediction (Fig. 1 of the paper): Omega vs m_a with blue (T2=100 MeV) and green (T2=500 MeV) bands reflecting instanton-computation uncertainty. Traced the LOWER edge of the combined band (blue band lower edge, running just below/along the dashed lattice line). Region above the band at fixed mass corresponds to DM overproduction for masses below the crossing with the dotted Omega_DM=0.258 line (~30-60 ueV). Hint suggested AxionMass (f_a vs m_a), but the actual plotted axes are m_a [ueV] vs Omega; per the plotted-values contract, y values are emitted as Omega, unconverted. Boundary is a straight power law on log-log (slope ~ -1.28), so uniform log sampling used.
